newsitem.title: FRENCH GUIANA: Ariane rocket launch delayed.
newsitem.headline: Ariane rocket launch delayed.

text.p: A technical problem aboard Western Europe's 94th Ariane rocket has delayed its scheduled February 25 launch by two days, space officials said on Wednesday.

"During the Flight 94 preparation campaign in Kourou (French Guiana) and according to its strict quality control policy, Arianespace has decided to replace on the ground system equipment the connecting plate of the liquid hydrogen umbilical arm," the Paris-based Arianespace company said in a statement.
"This will now lead to a launch during the night of February 27 to 28, 1997," it said.
The Ariane-4 rocket is scheduled to launch the INTELSAT 801 satellite for the Washington-based International Telecommunictions Satellite Organisation (INTELSAT).
The satellite is the 14th INTELSAT satellite to be launched aboard an Ariane rocket.
The Ariane rocket series is launched from the European Space Agency (ESA) launch centre in Kourou, French Guiana on the northeast coast of South America.
Arianespace leads the commercial satellite launch market and has successfully placed into orbit 17 heavy satellites since January 1996 aboard 11 Ariane rockets.
The company said its launch backlog is 40 satellites worth an estimated $3.4 billion.
